## [2.49.61] - 2026-05-22

**Schema version:** 56
**Commit summary:** **Wake sleeping creatures on damage — RAW Sleep ends the slumber when the sleeper takes damage.** Closes the v2.49.58 "wake-on-damage" filed item. New helper `_wake_sleeping_on_damage` called from both branches of `_apply_damage_to_combatant`. Scoped tightly: only removes Unconscious buffs with `source_spell == "Sleep"` — other Unconscious sources (future Power Word Knockout, future druid Sleep Touch, etc.) are left alone. Zero-damage hits (resistance reduced to 0) don't wake. Emits a public 🌅 roll-log entry so the GM + table see the cause. Same commit fixes a pre-existing latent bug in `_resistance_halve`: condition buffs (Paralyzed, Stunned, Sleep-Unconscious) carry `effects` as a string list, but the function assumed dict; it now skips non-dict effects. Bug had been latent since the first condition buff shipped because no prior test damaged a creature carrying a condition buff. 3 new harness tests + the latent-bug fix. PATCH — additive hook + bug fix; no API contract change.
**Description:** Three edits + one new test file. **(1)** `app/routes/tabletop_routes.py::_wake_sleeping_on_damage` (NEW helper, ~80 lines). Body: looks up the target combatant in hub state by `character_id` (PC) or `combatant_id` (NPC), filters buffs to those with key in (`unconscious`, `asleep`) AND `source_spell == "Sleep"`, removes them. PC path routes through `_remove_buff` (buff_update broadcast + paired-cleanup, no-op for concentration=False); NPC path mutates the buff list directly + broadcasts `battle_update` with `force_gm_sync=True` (mirrors v2.49.40 NPC HP-damage pattern). PC also calls `_mirror_buffs_to_sheet` so the sheet doesn't carry stale `_buffs_active` entries. Public 🌅 roll-log entry fires after the removal. Short-circuits on `damage_applied <= 0` and on missing target. **(2)** `app/routes/tabletop_routes.py::_apply_damage_to_combatant` — added `await _wake_sleeping_on_damage(...)` call in both branches, after the damage broadcast. **(3)** `app/routes/tabletop_routes.py::_resistance_halve` — guard `effects` with `isinstance(effects, dict)` before calling `.get("resistance_to")`. **(4)** `tests/harness/test_sleep_wake_on_damage.py` (NEW, 3 tests).
**Description (cont):** Why the helper at the damage-pipeline level, not at the buff-install level. The wake check is a *consequence* of damage, not a property of the buff. Putting the logic inside `_install_buff` or `_remove_buff` would put a "check for damage application" check inside a buff-state primitive — wrong direction of dependency. The damage pipeline is the right call site: every damage source (weapon attack, spell damage, AoE save-for-half, GM manual HP edit through future endpoints) routes through `_apply_damage_to_combatant`, so wiring the hook there covers every wake path with one call site per branch.
**Description (cont 2):** Why scope to `source_spell == "Sleep"` rather than wake on every Unconscious. Sleep's RAW "damage wakes" rule is spell-specific — it's listed in Sleep's text, not in the Unconscious condition's text. A future "Power Word Knockout" or "Druid Sleep Touch" or a homebrew "permanent magical slumber" might install Unconscious with different wake-on-damage semantics (or none — Power Word Knockout RAW is permanent until ended by another spell). The conservative default is to only fire the wake on the exact RAW source. Future endpoints add their own source_spell tags and the helper can be extended.
**Description (cont 3):** Why the `_resistance_halve` latent-bug fix lands in the same commit. The new wake tests are the first to apply damage to a PC carrying a condition buff (Sleep-Unconscious, with `effects: list`). When the damage handler called `_resistance_halve(damage, type, sheet)`, the function iterated `sheet["_buffs_active"]` and tried `effects.get("resistance_to")` — but `effects` was a list. AttributeError → 500. The fix (skip non-dict effects) is two lines; it's a precondition for the wake test to pass. Could ship as a separate commit, but the bug is tightly coupled to the test's damage path — splitting would land "test fails on latent bug" + "fix the latent bug, test now passes" in two commits when one tells the story cleanly.
**Description (cont 4):** Why the latent bug never tripped before. Resistance only applies when the target's sheet has `_buffs_active` entries — the only paths that populate that field are buffs installed via `_install_buff` + `_mirror_buffs_to_sheet`. Condition buffs (Paralyzed, Stunned, Unconscious-from-Sleep) DO go through that path. But the buff installs in test scenarios were never followed by a damage application: test_incapacitation_drops_concentration ends after the Paralyzed install (no damage), test_use_stunning_strike ends after Stunned (no damage), test_cast_sleep ends after Unconscious (no damage). The wake-on-damage test is the FIRST to combine "install a condition buff" + "deal damage to the wearer" in the same test. The bug was waiting for this exact pattern.
**Description (cont 5):** Why the 🌅 wake log is `Visibility.PUBLIC`, not GM-only. Concentration logs (💀, ✋, 🔁) are GM-only because concentration is a private mechanical detail the wizard tracks. Sleep wake-on-damage is a TABLE-VISIBLE event — the bandit was sleeping, you attacked, the table sees a roll, the bandit visibly snaps awake. Hiding that from the players makes the round confusing ("wait, is the bandit asleep or not?"). Public log keeps the table in sync with the canvas.
**Description (cont 6):** Test design. All three tests pre-seed the buff via `/battle` PUT rather than going through `/cast_sleep` end-to-end. Two reasons: (a) deterministic — the wake test doesn't care which combinations of HP / pool roll land the Sleep; the install path is already pinned by `test_cast_sleep.py`. (b) faster — no retry loop on the install. The attack retry loop is still required because hit-roll is random vs target AC; 20 iterations is the same pattern used by the v2.49.55 Stunning Strike happy-path NPC test. Reads the latest state via `gm_ws.buffered("battle_update")[-1]` (the wake fires AFTER the damage broadcast — both arrive in the buffer, the wake one is last). Initially the test used `wait_for("battle_update")` which always returns `hits[0]` (first match in buffer, not next); the bug was caught and fixed by switching to `buffered()[-1]`.
**Description (cont 7):** Verification. Pre-fix: NPC wake test failed with "buff still on bandit"; PC wake test failed with 500 (`_resistance_halve` AttributeError on `effects.get`). Post-fix (both `_wake_sleeping_on_damage` + `_resistance_halve` guard): all 3 wake tests pass. Full regression: 265 harness tests pass (was 262, +3 new); no regressions on existing damage / buff / concentration tests.

### Added
- `app/routes/tabletop_routes.py::_wake_sleeping_on_damage` — new helper called from both branches of `_apply_damage_to_combatant`. Removes Sleep-sourced Unconscious buffs + emits a public 🌅 wake log.
- `tests/harness/test_sleep_wake_on_damage.py` — 3 tests (NPC wake / PC wake / non-Sleep unconscious preserved).
- `docs/test-harness-coverage.md` — catalog entry; total 262 → 265.

### Fixed
- `app/routes/tabletop_routes.py::_resistance_halve` — guards `effects` against being a list before calling `.get("resistance_to")`. Pre-existing latent bug exposed by the new wake test (first to apply damage to a wearer of a condition buff). All condition buffs (Paralyzed, Stunned, Unconscious-from-Sleep, Charmed, Frightened) carry `effects` as a string list; mechanical buffs (Rage, Hex, Hunter's Mark) carry it as a dict. The check now correctly applies only to dict-shaped effects.

### Notes
- **Backward compat.** Pure additive hook + pure defensive guard. No API contract change; no broadcast shape change beyond the new (additive) 🌅 roll-log entry.
- **Fifth use of the buff-source filter.** Three previous sites filter buffs by `source_char_id` (v2.49.51 / v2.49.53 / v2.49.54). This commit filters by `source_spell` — same semantic shape ("this buff is mine to act on") but keyed on the SPELL name rather than the CASTER. Both filter dimensions matter going forward; codifying them under a single helper would dedupe across all five sites.
- **Public 🌅 visibility, not GM-only.** Wake-on-damage is table-visible (the table sees a damage roll + a sleeper waking); concentration events (💀, ✋, 🔁) are GM-only because concentration is a private detail.

### Filed
- **`source_spell` filter helper** — five sites now filter buffs by some combination of `source_char_id` / `source_spell`. A `_is_own_buff_for(buff, character_id=None, spell_name=None)` helper would dedupe. Punt unless a sixth site lands.
- **Wake-via-shake action** — RAW Sleep also wakes a sleeper when another creature uses an action to shake them. Needs a new `/shake_awake` endpoint (action consumption + remove Sleep-Unconscious from target). Filed for follow-up; for now GM clears via `/end_buff unconscious`.
- **Resistance for condition buffs** — would condition buffs ever advertise damage resistance? Hideous Laughter's prone-and-incapacitated doesn't. Stoneskin (separate spell) installs resistance via a mechanical-effect buff with `effects: dict`. The two shapes are RAW-distinct, so no future condition needs to advertise resistance. The dict-check guard is correct.
- **Undead / immune-to-charm exclusion for Sleep targeting** — still open from v2.49.58.

## [2.49.60] - 2026-05-21

**Schema version:** 56
**Commit summary:** **Add a "restart the app container after every version bump" rule to CLAUDE.md.** Doc-only. The docker dev image bakes the code at build time (no live-reload mount on the `app` service in `docker-compose.yml`), which means a committed version bump doesn't propagate to the running container until `docker compose up -d --build app` runs. Surfaced during this session when the v2.49.55 Stunning Strike endpoint worked but `/version` reported v2.49.54 — the container had been built between commits, leaving the visible version stale. Documenting the rebuild as an explicit step in the per-commit workflow makes it impossible to forget AND surfaces the rationale (harness tests at `http://localhost:8013` talk to the container, not in-process code; a stale container masks new-endpoint regressions and inline-migration runs). Rule lives next to the existing "Always create the git commit at the end of the change" rule because both describe the per-commit deploy cadence. PATCH — docs-only.
**Description:** One edit. **(1)** `CLAUDE.md` — new paragraph "Restart the app container after every version bump" appended to the "Always update the changelog and version when making changes" section. Names the rebuild command (`docker compose up -d --build app`), the verification command (`curl -s http://localhost:8013/version`), and the expected timing (5–15 s on Apple Silicon). Calls out three failure modes the rebuild prevents: (a) harness tests against stale code returning 404 for new endpoints, (b) manual click-through verification on stale code, (c) `SCHEMA_VERSION` bumps that leave the DB un-migrated because `_apply_inline_migrations` only fires on container boot. Warns against `docker compose down -v` as a destructive workaround (would wipe the postgres volume + the demo seed has known FK-ordering bugs on partial-state replays).
**Description (cont):** Why CLAUDE.md rather than a settings.json hook. The user explicitly requested adding the rule to "your claude file" — they want this as a behavioral guideline I read at the start of every session, not a harness-executed automation. A pre/post-commit hook would be more reliable (no chance of me forgetting) but adds complexity: the hook would have to detect a version bump (parse `version.py`), then run a 30-second docker rebuild as part of the commit cycle, blocking the next prompt. CLAUDE.md keeps the rule visible without coupling the rebuild to the commit lifecycle — I run it explicitly after each commit instead.
**Description (cont 2):** Why the rule applies to doc-only commits too. The temptation is to skip the rebuild when "no code changed" — but `version.py` IS code (`APP_VERSION` is imported by `/version`, `/healthz`, and the runtime banner). A doc-only commit that bumps `APP_VERSION` leaves the running container reporting the OLD version, which is wrong for any observer (browser client polling for updates, harness asserting on `/version`, GM looking at the banner). The rule is universal — "every version bump = rebuild" — to avoid carving out exceptions that drift.
**Description (cont 3):** Verification. Pre-fix: CLAUDE.md had no rebuild guidance; the docker container could (and did) lag the source repo by several commits without warning. Post-fix: the rule lives in CLAUDE.md and is the second-to-last paragraph in the version-management section — the natural reading order is "bump → CHANGELOG → README → commit → restart." Doc-only; no functional change. Container restart performed as part of this commit per the new rule.

### Added
- `CLAUDE.md` — new "Restart the app container after every version bump" paragraph in the version-management section. Names the rebuild command + verification command + three failure modes the rule prevents.

### Notes
- **Backward compat.** Doc-only. No code changes.
- **Self-applying.** This commit itself bumps the version, so the rule kicks in immediately — the container is rebuilt as part of landing this commit.

## [2.49.58] - 2026-05-21

**Schema version:** 56
**Commit summary:** **Add the Sleep spell — custom HP-pool targeting.** Closes the "Sleep — still absent" filed item from v2.49.55–v2.49.57. RAW (PHB Sleep, 1st-level enchantment, bard/sorcerer/warlock/wizard): roll 5d8 (+2d8 per slot level above 1st) as an HP pool; sort candidate creatures by ascending current HP, ignoring already-unconscious ones; walk the list and put each affected creature to sleep, subtracting their HP from the pool, until the pool is exhausted or there are no candidates left. No save, no concentration. New endpoint `POST /cast_sleep` (dedicated, NOT routed through `/cast_spell` because the HP-pool selector doesn't fit either save-or-suck or save-for-half). The Unconscious key is already in `_INCAPACITATING_BUFF_KEYS`, so a PC sleeper drops their own concentration via the v2.49.51 hook + emits 💀 — the test pins this end-to-end for the first time on the no-save install path. Also adds Sleep to Thalindra's demo spell list (appended, so existing FIREBALL_INDEX = 7 / Counterspell index assumptions in other harness tests stay intact). 8 new harness tests pin the pool math + ordering invariant + drop-concentration hook + 409 paths. PATCH — additive endpoint + additive seed-list entry; no existing routes or shapes change.
**Description:** Three edits + one new test file. **(1)** `app/routes/tabletop_routes.py::cast_sleep` (NEW). Body: `{character_id, class_slug, slot_level, target_combatant_ids, override?}`. Validates class (wizard/bard/sorcerer/warlock) + Sleep on the spell list + slot at requested level + Phase 4 action gate (overrideable). Rolls 5d8 + 2d8/level, resolves targets via `_lookup_combatant`, skips already-unconscious + zero-HP, sorts ascending, walks the list installing `unconscious` buffs via `_install_buff` (PC) or `_install_buff_on_combatant_id` (NPC). Marks the action slot + broadcasts a public `roll` event naming the pool + affected list + a `spell_slot_update`. **(2)** `app/demo_seed.py::_wizard_sheet` — appended Sleep to Thalindra's spells. Existing `FIREBALL_INDEX = 7` and Counterspell index references in harness tests are preserved because Sleep lands at index 10 (or 9 in any DB missing Lightning Bolt). **(3)** `tests/harness/test_cast_sleep.py` (NEW, 8 tests).
**Description (cont):** Why a dedicated endpoint rather than routing through `/cast_spell`. Sleep is the only PHB 5e spell with HP-pool targeting; there's no second spell that would amortize a generalized pipeline. `/cast_spell` already branches on save-or-suck vs. save-for-half vs. attack-roll vs. AoE; adding a fifth "HP-pool" branch would tangle the cast-spell handler further. Dedicated endpoint (~280 LOC vs. ~50 LOC of branching in cast_spell, but isolated) follows the cast_hex pattern: Hex also doesn't fit cast_spell's generic shape (unique concentration-buff effects + ability picker).
**Description (cont 2):** Why dice-independent assertions in the ordering test. The pool roll is 5d8 — min 5, max 40, avg 22.5. Asserting a specific affected count would flake. Instead the ordering test asserts the invariants that hold for ANY pool ≥ 5: (a) non-decreasing HP order in `affected`, (b) `sum(affected.hp) <= pool_total`, (c) first `unaffected` (if any) has `hp > pool_remaining` at stop time. Pool=5 → 1+2 affected (3 unaffected); pool=20 → all 3 affected. Both satisfy all three invariants. The "happy path NPC" test uses HP=5 + 5d8 (min=5) for a single-target always-affected case — guaranteed without invariant trickery.
**Description (cont 3):** Why already-unconscious targets are skipped entirely (not "added to unaffected"). RAW: "Creatures within 20 feet of a point you choose within range are affected in ascending order of their current hit points (**ignoring unconscious creatures**)." Skipped from the ordering AND the response — the spell doesn't waste pool on already-asleep creatures, and the response shouldn't report them as "not affected" (which would imply they were considered). The test asserts the already-unconscious bandit appears in neither `affected` nor `unaffected` — clear semantics for the cast-card UI.
**Description (cont 4):** Why this pins the v2.49.51 hook for the third time, and what's new about this branch. v2.49.51 covers the hook generically. The two prior end-to-end tests pin it for: (a) Hold Person (concentration=True, save-or-suck via /cast_spell PC roll_request), (b) Stunning Strike (concentration=False, save-or-suck via /use_stunning_strike PC roll_request). Sleep is the **first no-save** path: the install isn't gated on a saving throw; Thalindra picks the targets and they sleep based on pool math. The hook fires the same way (key="unconscious" matches `_INCAPACITATING_BUFF_KEYS`), but exercised through the no-save call site rather than the save-or-suck pipeline. Reaffirms that the hook is install-site-agnostic.
**Description (cont 5):** Why Thalindra's seed list adds Sleep at the END. Existing harness tests reference `FIREBALL_INDEX = 7` and other hardcoded spell positions. Inserting Sleep at index 3 (next to Magic Missile, alphabetical-by-level) would shift Fireball to index 8 and break every cast-spell-aoe test. Appending keeps every existing index stable.
**Description (cont 6):** What's NOT modelled here. **Undead / immune-to-charm exclusion** — RAW excludes undead + creatures immune to charm. SimpleVTT doesn't track creature-type immunities consistently, so v1 trusts the GM to deselect inappropriate targets via the candidate-list input. **Wake-on-damage** — RAW: "the sleeper takes damage [...] [wakes them] awake." The existing damage pipeline doesn't auto-clear the Unconscious buff on damage; the GM runs `/end_buff unconscious` manually. **Wake-via-shake** — no `/shake_awake` endpoint; `/end_buff unconscious` covers it for now. **20-ft radius enforcement** — no spatial range yet; the candidate list IS the radius from the GM's perspective (filed as coupled to the ruler/range work being planned separately).
**Description (cont 7):** Verification. Ran the new tests pre-fix: all 8 failed with 404 (endpoint missing) + 409 spell_not_known (Sleep not on Thalindra's list). Post-fix: all 8 pass. Full regression: 262 harness tests pass total (was 254, +8 new) — one pre-existing flaky attack-crit test occasionally trips; not my doing and not load-bearing. 33 encounter-sim tests unchanged.

### Added
- `app/routes/tabletop_routes.py::cast_sleep` — new endpoint `POST /api/campaign/{cid}/cast_sleep`. Validates class + Sleep on list + slot + Phase 4 gate; rolls 5d8 + 2d8/level pool; sorts targets by ascending current HP, skips already-unconscious; walks the list installing Unconscious via `_install_buff` (PC) / `_install_buff_on_combatant_id` (NPC).
- `app/demo_seed.py::_wizard_sheet` — Sleep appended to Thalindra's spell list (`_slug: "sleep"`, level 1, prepared, 1 action). Appended to preserve existing harness spell-index references.
- `tests/harness/test_cast_sleep.py` — 8 tests (happy path NPC / ordering invariant / high HP skip / already-unconscious skip / drops PC concentration / upcast scales pool / no_slot / wrong_class).
- `docs/test-harness-coverage.md` — catalog entry; total 254 → 262.

### Notes
- **Backward compat.** Pure additive: new endpoint, new seed-list entry appended at the end. Existing `/cast_spell` behavior + every other endpoint unchanged. Existing harness `FIREBALL_INDEX = 7` / Counterspell index assumptions preserved by appending Sleep.
- **Third install-site for the v2.49.51 hook.** First was Hold Person (concentration=True save-or-suck PC), second was Stunning Strike (concentration=False save-or-suck PC), third is Sleep (no-save, no concentration, install-by-pool-math). Same hook fires; same 💀 log emits; install-site-agnostic.
- **Dice path uses the seeded RNG.** `dice_mod.roll("5d8")` honors the `DICE_SEED` env var so seeded test runs would be deterministic. The harness tests assert dice-independent invariants anyway — no DICE_SEED needed.

- **Undead / immune-to-charm exclusion** — needs creature-type tagging on monster templates to enforce automatically. v1 trusts the GM to deselect inappropriate targets.
- **Wake-on-damage** — when a sleeper takes damage, RAW wakes them. The damage pipeline could check for `unconscious` source=`Sleep` and call `_remove_buff` after applying damage. Out of scope here.
- **Wake-via-shake** — `/shake_awake` endpoint that takes another creature's action to wake a sleeping ally. Or just `/end_buff unconscious` for now.
- **20-ft radius enforcement** — coupled to the ruler/range planning work. Currently the candidate list IS the radius.
- **Bard / Sorcerer / Warlock spell lists** — Sleep is RAW on all four lists but only Thalindra's demo seed has it. Add to Lyra (Bard), Zara (Sorcerer), Magnus (Warlock) so all eligible classes can demo the spell. Trivial follow-up.
- **Open Hand Technique PC tests** — carried forward from v2.49.57.

## [2.49.57] - 2026-05-21

**Schema version:** 56
**Commit summary:** **Add Monk Open Hand Technique (Way of the Open Hand, Lv 3+ subclass feature).** Closes the "Open Hand Technique" filed item from v2.49.55. RAW: when monk hits with a Flurry of Blows attack, they may impose one of three riders — Prone (DEX save), Push 15 ft (STR save), or No Reactions (no save, 1 turn). No additional ki cost (the Flurry already paid). New endpoint `POST /use_open_hand_technique` takes a `mode` param (`prone` | `push` | `no_reactions`). Prone routes through the save-or-suck pipeline using a new `open-hand-prone` entry in `_SPELL_CONDITION_MAP`. Push uses the same pipeline structurally but has NO map entry — the response carries `push_authorized` so the GM UI can drag the token; no buff installs. No Reactions skips the save entirely and installs a `reaction-denied` buff inline (`concentration: False`, `duration_rounds: 1`) plus a public roll-log entry. 5 new harness tests pin all three modes + 409 wrong_class + 400 bad_mode. PATCH — additive endpoint; existing routes and broadcast shapes unchanged.
**Description:** Three edits. **(1)** `app/routes/tabletop_routes.py::_SPELL_CONDITION_MAP` — added `"open-hand-prone"` entry. `key: "prone"`, `concentration: False`, `duration_rounds: 10` (Prone has no RAW timer — ends when the prone creature spends half movement to stand; 10 rounds is a generous default and the GM ends it via `/end_buff`). Effects list summarizes the RAW prone-condition rider. Crucially **not** in `_INCAPACITATING_BUFF_KEYS` — Prone constrains movement / grants advantage at melee + disadvantage at range, but doesn't incapacitate. **(2)** `app/routes/tabletop_routes.py::use_open_hand_technique` — new `POST /api/campaign/{cid}/use_open_hand_technique` endpoint. Validates monk + Way of the Open Hand + Lv 3+. Branches on `mode`: no_reactions is the early-return inline-install path (mirrors `/use_rage` / `/use_bardic_inspiration` "install + announce"); prone + push share the save pipeline (same DC math + roll_request setup as Stunning Strike). **(3)** `tests/harness/test_use_open_hand_technique.py` (NEW, 5 tests).
**Description (cont):** Why one endpoint with a `mode` param rather than three separate endpoints. RAW the three options are one feature with one "choose at use time" gate. Splitting into `/use_open_hand_prone` / `/use_open_hand_push` / `/use_open_hand_no_reactions` would triple the validation boilerplate (monk + subclass + level + target lookup all repeat) and force three almost-identical chat-card buttons. A single endpoint with a discriminator keeps the validation in one place + matches how the future UI surfaces the feature (one button with a popover that picks the mode). The mode whitelist (`prone` / `push` / `no_reactions`) is the same shape as `class_slug` parameters on existing multi-class spell-cast endpoints.
**Description (cont 2):** Why push has no `_SPELL_CONDITION_MAP` entry. Push doesn't install a buff — it grants the monk permission to physically move the target up to 15 ft. SimpleVTT today doesn't enforce movement, so the push is a GM-facing "drag the token" instruction. The response carries `push_authorized: True` (on save fail) / `False` (on pass) so the cast-card UI can render a "Drag target up to 15 ft from monk" prompt. For PC targets the save is rolled by the player via roll_request; the GM observes the save total in the roll log and acts (the /respond handler's install branch is a no-op because `_SPELL_CONDITION_MAP.get("open-hand-push")` is None). For NPC targets the server rolls inline and `push_authorized` ships in the same response.
**Description (cont 3):** Why no_reactions skips the save pipeline entirely. RAW has no save — the rider just lands. Routing through the save-or-suck pipeline would mean creating a sham DC=0 roll_request with no decision branches; cleaner to install inline + broadcast a public roll-log entry. Mirrors the no-save inline-install path in `/use_rage` (rage buff lands without a roll) and `/use_bardic_inspiration` (inspiration die buff lands without a roll). The `reaction-denied` buff key is custom (not a standard 5e condition) — `_SPELL_CONDITION_MAP` doesn't help here because there's no roll outcome to gate on; the buff dict is constructed inline.
**Description (cont 4):** Subclass validation. Sheet stores `"subclass": "Way of the Open Hand"`. Endpoint normalizes via `(sheet.get("subclass") or "").lower()` and checks `"open hand" in subclass`. Substring-match keeps the gate forgiving for cosmetic variations ("Way of The Open Hand", "Open Hand Tradition", etc.) while still rejecting other monk subclasses ("Way of Shadow", "Way of the Four Elements"). 409 `wrong_subclass` with `expected: "way of the open hand"` and `got: <whatever the sheet says>` so the UI can render a helpful error.
**Description (cont 5):** Test strategy. NPC happy paths (prone + push) use the same retry-loop pattern as the Stunning Strike NPC happy path because the save is random. The push test asserts the inverse-correlation invariant (`push_authorized == not auto_save_passed`) which is a single-iteration check — push is interesting in both branches. No_reactions is deterministic (no roll) — single-call assert. wrong_class + bad_mode are deterministic error-paths.
**Description (cont 6):** Verification. Ran the new tests pre-fix: all 5 failed with 404. Post-fix: all 5 pass. Full regression: 254 harness tests pass (was 249, +5 new); 33 encounter-sim tests still pass.

### Added
- `app/routes/tabletop_routes.py::_SPELL_CONDITION_MAP["open-hand-prone"]` — new entry with `key: "prone"`, `concentration: False`, `duration_rounds: 10`. NOT in `_INCAPACITATING_BUFF_KEYS` (Prone doesn't incapacitate RAW).
- `app/routes/tabletop_routes.py::use_open_hand_technique` — new endpoint `POST /api/campaign/{cid}/use_open_hand_technique`. Validates monk + Way of the Open Hand + Lv 3+. Modes: `prone`, `push`, `no_reactions`.

- **PC roll_request paths.** Prone PC routes through the same `_save_request_context` + `/respond` install pipeline as Stunning Strike PC (already pinned by `test_stunning_strike_pc_drops_own_concentration`). Push PC stashes a context with `spell_slug: "open-hand-push"` which has no map entry — `/respond`'s install branch is a no-op by design. End-to-end PC tests for Open Hand are filed below.
- **No "must follow Flurry hit" enforcement.** Same trust-the-caller convention as Stunning Strike. UI is expected to gate the button on the most-recent Flurry hit outcome.

Push PC needs a new assertion shape (the /respond handler doesn't install a buff but the GM should still see the save total in the roll log). No-reactions PC mirrors the no-save NPC test with a PC target. All three are similar enough that one combined PC test could cover the file.

## [2.49.55] - 2026-05-21

**Schema version:** 56
**Commit summary:** **Add Monk Stunning Strike (Lv 5+ class feature) — first non-concentration incapacitating buff endpoint.** Closes the "Stunning Strike endpoint missing" item filed in v2.49.51. RAW: monk hits with a melee attack, spends 1 ki, target makes CON save (DC = 8 + monk prof + monk WIS mod), on fail Stunned until end of monk's next turn. Stunned is RAW `concentration: False` (1-turn condition, not a sustained spell) — so this commit also validates the v2.49.51 incapacitation hook's "concentration=False" branch end-to-end: the Stunned install on a PC target via the existing roll_request → /respond pipeline drops the PC's own concentration anchors via the `_install_buff` v2.49.51 path. Endpoint reuses the cast_spell save-or-suck pipeline by routing through `_SPELL_CONDITION_MAP["stunning-strike"]` (new entry, slug treated as a class-feature identifier — the lookup is slug-keyed and doesn't care whether the source is a spell or a feature). NPC targets get a server-rolled save inline. PC targets get a roll_request the player owner /responds to (same path as Hold Person). 3 new harness tests pin happy-path NPC + wrong_class + no_ki. PATCH — additive endpoint; existing routes and broadcast shapes unchanged.
**Description:** Three edits. **(1)** `app/routes/tabletop_routes.py::_SPELL_CONDITION_MAP` — added a new `"stunning-strike"` entry with `key: "stunned"`, `concentration: False`, `duration_rounds: 1`, RAW effects list. The slug is a class-feature identifier; the existing pipeline doesn't care whether it's a spell or a feature, just looks it up by slug. **(2)** `app/routes/tabletop_routes.py::use_stunning_strike` — new `POST /api/campaign/{cid}/use_stunning_strike` endpoint. Body: `{character_id, target_combatant_id?, target_character_id?, target_name?}`. Validates monk class + level >= 5 + ki >= 1, then spends 1 ki, computes save DC = 8 + monk prof + monk WIS mod, and routes through either the NPC server-rolled save path (mirrors cast_spell line ~7440) or the PC roll_request path (mirrors line ~7392). On fail the existing save-or-suck install code at line ~6564 picks up the slug from `_save_request_context` and installs Stunned via `_install_buff` (PC) / `_install_buff_on_combatant_id` (NPC inline above). Stunning Strike is a free interrupt RAW, so no action / bonus / reaction slot is consumed (only ki). **(3)** `tests/harness/test_use_stunning_strike.py` (NEW, 3 tests).
**Description (cont):** Why route through `_SPELL_CONDITION_MAP` rather than write a bespoke install. The save-or-suck pipeline already handles three coupled concerns: (a) the DC computation + save-roll broadcast + result correlation back to the cast card, (b) the buff dict construction with correct source/duration/concentration/effects, (c) the v2.49.51 incapacitation hook firing via `_install_buff`. Reusing the pipeline keeps Stunning Strike consistent with Hold Person etc.: a future GM-facing "save events" filter will surface stuns the same way it surfaces hold-persons. Cost: a slug naming convention that conflates "spell" and "class feature." Acceptable trade.
**Description (cont 2):** Why Stunning Strike is the right first non-concentration incapacitating impl. Alternatives considered: **Sleep** — 1d8-per-slot HP pool affects creatures by ascending HP, no save, unique selection mechanic that doesn't fit any existing endpoint pattern; would need a custom targeting flow (~3× the LOC). **Power Word Stun** — 150-HP threshold then 1-CHA-save mechanic, narrower use case, requires high-level seed setup. **Banishment** — RAW debatable on incapacitation; impl in SimpleVTT today is removal-from-init (different code path entirely). Stunning Strike: single-target, CON save, simple ki cost, monk already in demo, fits the existing save-or-suck pipeline, validates the v2.49.51 hook's non-concentration branch. Cleanest unit of work.
**Description (cont 3):** Why no slot consumption. RAW: "When you hit another creature with a melee weapon attack, you can spend 1 ki point to attempt a stunning strike." It's an interrupt that piggybacks on an attack, not an action of its own. The attack itself consumes the action; Stunning Strike is the rider. The endpoint enforces ki consumption but skips action / bonus / reaction marking. (Compare /use_lay_on_hands which marks the action slot — Lay on Hands IS the paladin's action, RAW.) The "must follow a hit" constraint is filed for the client-side UI (the chat-card "Stun?" button should only appear after a successful melee hit); the endpoint itself trusts the caller, matching the override-friendly convention of other class-feature endpoints.
**Description (cont 4):** Test strategy. The NPC happy path uses the same retry-loop pattern as `test_save_or_suck_installs_caster_concentration` because CON saves are random — DC depends on Kael's stats vs. the bandit's CON. 20 iterations gives plenty of failure odds. Verification uses the `battle_update` WS broadcast (since there's no `/battle` GET endpoint — combatant state is hub-resident and surfaces via WS or via the `/buffs` GET on PC characters; NPC buffs only via WS). The test asserts (a) endpoint response shape, (b) buff key + `concentration: False` + `source_char_id` on the broadcast buff, (c) WS `battle_update` envelope. The 409 paths are deterministic (no dice) — single-call assertions.
**Description (cont 5):** Verification. Ran the new tests pre-fix: all 3 failed with 404 ("endpoint not found"). Post-fix: all 3 pass. Full regression: 248 harness tests pass (was 245, +3 new); 33 encounter-sim tests still pass.

- `app/routes/tabletop_routes.py::use_stunning_strike` — new endpoint `POST /api/campaign/{cid}/use_stunning_strike`. Validates monk + Lv 5 + ki >= 1. Spends 1 ki. Routes through the save-or-suck pipeline.

## [2.49.54] - 2026-05-21

**Schema version:** 56
**Commit summary:** **Fix RAW bug: swap loop wrongly dropped paired conditions from other casters.** Closes the bug filed in v2.49.53. PHB p.203 RAW: "you can only concentrate on ONE spell at a time" applies per-caster. A paired condition buff on a victim — e.g. Paralyzed on a Hold Person victim, where `source_char_id` is the enemy caster — is sustained by the SOURCE caster's concentration, not the victim's. The victim casting a new concentration spell of their own should NOT drop the paired condition (otherwise a Held victim could "shake off" being Held by casting Hex, which is wrong RAW + bad gameplay). Pre-fix, `_install_buff`'s swap loop dropped every `concentration: True` buff on the combatant when a new concentration buff landed, regardless of who sourced the existing ones. v2.49.53 already added the source filter to the 🔁 log emission (so the audit was correct); v2.49.54 applies the same filter to the underlying BEHAVIOR so the buff is preserved, not just the log. The fix is a 5-line addition inside the swap loop: when `b.get("source_char_id")` is non-null and != self, append the buff to `new_list` instead of marking it as replaced. 2 new harness tests pin the new behavior + a regression guard for legitimate own-anchor swaps. PATCH — bug fix; no schema or API contract change.
**Description:** Two edits + one new test file. **(1)** `app/routes/tabletop_routes.py::_install_buff` swap loop — inside the `if is_concentration and b.get("concentration"):` branch, added a new check before marking the buff as replaced: if `b.get("source_char_id")` is non-null AND != `character_id`, append the buff to `new_list` (preserve it) and `continue` instead of falling through to the replace path. This filter mirrors the one already applied to (a) `_drop_caster_concentration` (v2.49.51) and (b) the v2.49.53 🔁 log emission — three places now share the same "is this buff actually owned by this combatant?" predicate. **(2)** `tests/harness/test_swap_preserves_paired_buffs.py` (NEW, 2 tests).
**Description (cont):** Why the fix landed via the swap loop rather than upstream. The bug class is: "concentration-flagged buffs on a combatant might be owned by them OR by someone else." Every code path that iterates `target.get("buffs")` and treats `concentration: True` as "this combatant's anchor" has the same bug latent in it. v2.49.51 fixed `_drop_caster_concentration`. v2.49.53 fixed the 🔁 log. v2.49.54 fixes the swap loop. The remaining sites: `_concentration_buff_for` (used by `_maybe_concentration_save`) — also has the bug latent but a paired-condition victim taking damage and rolling a "CON save" for someone else's concentration spell is an edge case worth filing separately. Tracked in the Filed section below.
**Description (cont 2):** Why a victim shouldn't be able to "drop" the paired condition by casting their own concentration spell. The Hold Person caster is the one sustaining the spell via their own concentration; what happens to THE VICTIM's concentration doesn't end the source caster's spell. The victim can't unilaterally end someone else's spell by casting their own — only the source caster's actions (damage taken → failed CON save, voluntary end, incapacitation, death) end Hold Person. If the victim could end the paired buff by casting their own concentration spell, that'd be a major gameplay break.
**Description (cont 3):** Why a regression guard for own-anchor swap. The source filter narrows the swap-loop drop condition. The risk in narrowing is over-narrowing: if the filter accidentally protected own anchors too, casting a new concentration spell wouldn't replace the old one — broken RAW one-at-a-time. The regression test pre-seeds Magnus with `concentration-bless` (source=Magnus), casts Hex, and asserts the anchor was DROPPED. Without this test, an over-broad filter (e.g. `if b.get("source_char_id") is not None` without the `!= self` clause) would silently regress all swaps.
**Description (cont 4):** Why this isn't catching a real incident yet. The current demo doesn't have a flow that triggers the bug naturally — to be a Hold Person victim AND cast a new concentration spell, the victim has to first be paralyzed (which incapacitates them, blocking spell casting). Sleep / Suggestion / Calm Emotions are non-incapacitating concentration spells that leave the victim able to cast — but those aren't in the demo. The bug was discovered while writing v2.49.53's harness test setup (which deliberately constructs a paired-buff scenario via `/battle` PUT to bypass the can't-cast-while-paralyzed gate). Filing the fix now keeps the rule semantically correct ahead of future spell additions.
**Description (cont 5):** Verification. Ran `test_paired_buff_preserved_when_caster_swaps` pre-fix: failed (Paralyzed dropped from Magnus's buff list after Hex install). Post-fix: passes (both buffs co-exist). `test_own_anchor_swap_still_works` passed both before and after — the regression guard. Full regression: 245 harness tests pass (was 243, +2 new); 33 encounter-sim tests still pass. No existing tests touched the bug condition so no surprise breakages.

### Fixed
- `app/routes/tabletop_routes.py::_install_buff` swap loop — applies the `source_char_id is None or == character_id` filter inside the swap branch. Paired condition buffs from other casters are now preserved when the combatant casts a new concentration spell. Matches the source filter already applied in `_drop_caster_concentration` (v2.49.51) and the 🔁 log emission (v2.49.53).

### Added
- `tests/harness/test_swap_preserves_paired_buffs.py` — 2 tests (paired-buff-preserved / own-anchor-still-replaces).
- `docs/test-harness-coverage.md` — catalog entry; total 243 → 245.

### Notes
- **Backward compat.** Pure behavior fix — no schema, broadcast shape, or response shape change. Existing callers and tests are unaffected (none triggered the bug condition because the demo lacks non-incapacitating concentration-spell-on-victim flows). The fix is forward-compatible with Sleep, Suggestion, Calm Emotions, etc.
- **Source-filter is now the canonical predicate**: `source_char_id is None or == character_id` means "this combatant is concentrating on this buff." Three call sites now use it: `_drop_caster_concentration` (v2.49.51), `_install_buff` 🔁 log (v2.49.53), `_install_buff` swap loop (this commit). If a fourth site emerges, refactor into a helper.

### Filed
- **`_concentration_buff_for` has the same latent bug** — it returns the first `concentration: True` buff on a combatant without checking source. Used by `_maybe_concentration_save` (the CON-save-on-damage path). Fix makes the incapacitation drop explicit + load-bearing: a new `_INCAPACITATING_BUFF_KEYS` frozenset enumerates the RAW-incapacitating condition keys (paralyzed / incapacitated / stunned / petrified / unconscious / asleep). When `_install_buff` lands one of these on a target, it snapshots the target's OWN concentration anchors BEFORE the replacement loop, lets the existing replacement run, then emits a 💀 GM-only log per anchor naming the incapacitating buff. If the incapacitating buff itself is `concentration: False` (e.g. future Sleep impl), the anchor is also explicitly removed via `_remove_buff` so the fix isn't dependent on the swap-by-concentration heuristic. `_drop_caster_concentration` is refined to filter by `source_char_id` so paired condition buffs from other casters aren't swept when the helper fires (death-save callers also benefit — dead PC drops only their own anchors, not paired conditions another caster is concentrating on them with). 3 new harness tests pin the new behavior + a regression guard for the v2.38.0 paired-cleanup path. Charmed and Frightened deliberately excluded — those conditions constrain action choice but don't incapacitate per RAW. **(2)** `_install_buff` — before the existing replacement loop, computes `incapacitates_target = key in _INCAPACITATING_BUFF_KEYS and (src_of_new is None or src_of_new != character_id)` (the second clause skips the bizarre self-cast-Hideous-Laughter edge case), then snapshots `preexisting_own_anchors` (concentration-flagged buffs where `source_char_id` is None or == character_id — i.e. anchors the target is concentrating on, not paired conditions from other casters). After the existing replacement + paired-cleanup runs, if `incapacitates_target` AND `preexisting_own_anchors` is non-empty: for each anchor, (a) if it's still in `new_list` (incapacitating buff wasn't concentration=True so the swap didn't remove it), call `_remove_buff` to drop it cleanly; (b) emit a `type=roll` GM-only log with note `f"💀 {caster_name} lost concentration on {anchor_name}"` and breakdown `f"Concentration ends — incapacitated ({buff_label})"`. **(3)** `_drop_caster_concentration` — added `source_char_id` filter (`src is not None and src != character_id` → skip). **Description (cont 2):** Why both the "existing replacement already handles it" AND the new hook need to coexist. The existing replacement (line 411: `if is_concentration and b.get("concentration")`) drops Hex when Paralyzed lands because BOTH are flagged concentration. This is right outcome / wrong cause: the swap rule treats the victim as "switching" concentration spells, when RAW says they're losing it because they're incapacitated. Three reasons to add the explicit hook even though the visible outcome currently matches:

**Commit summary:** **Distinguish 💀 incapacitation drops from 💔 failed-save drops in the GM concentration log.** Closes the UI-tag follow-up filed in v2.49.48. Pre-fix, every concentration drop emitted the same `💔 NAME lost concentration on SPELL` log — failed CON save, 0-HP forced drop, death-save → dead, GM override → dead all looked identical to the GM. The 0-HP case was the most misleading: the save was still rolled (may have been a nat-20), but the log claimed it "failed." Fix splits the emoji + breakdown: 💔 = failed CON save (existing path), 💀 = incapacitated (0 HP or death-save-state transition). The broadcast shape is unchanged (still `type=roll` with `visibility=gm_only`); the cause distinction is in the note text + breakdown so existing handlers that filter on type+visibility continue to work. **Description:** Two file edits + one new test file. **(1)** `app/routes/tabletop_routes.py::_drop_caster_concentration` — accepts a new keyword-only ``reason: str = "incapacitated"`` param. Before calling `_remove_buff`, snapshots each concentration buff's key + name + paired-buff list (the cleanup helper mutates state in place, so reading after-the-fact returns empty paired lists). After successful removal, emits a `type=roll` GM-only log entry: `note=f"💀 {caster_name} lost concentration on {buff_name}{paired_note}"` + `breakdown=f"Concentration ends — {reason}"`. The caster name is read from `target.get("name")` (combatant display name, not character record). **(2)** `app/routes/tabletop_routes.py::_maybe_concentration_save` (the v2.49.48 0-HP forced-drop branch) — when `forced_drop_on_zero_hp=True`, switches emoji to 💀 and rewrites the breakdown to `"Concentration ends — incapacitated (0 HP) — save would have been 1d20[N]+M = X vs DC Y"`. The save text is preserved for telemetry so the GM can audit what the d20 was. **(3)** Both death-save callers now pass distinct reason strings: `roll_death_save` → `"3 failed death saves"`, `override_death_save` → `f"GM override → {status_in}"`. **(4)** `tests/harness/test_concentration_skull_log.py` (NEW, 4 tests).
**Description (cont):** Why a string ``reason`` param instead of an enum. The reason is purely human-readable log text — nothing downstream branches on it. An enum would force every caller to import + match on the value; a string lets each caller phrase the cause naturally and keeps `_drop_caster_concentration` agnostic to who's calling it. If a future commit needs structured cause data (e.g. for filtering the roll-log), the field can be added to the broadcast separately without rewriting the helper signature.
**Description (cont 2):** Why preserve the rolled save in the 0-HP breakdown. RAW says concentration ends regardless of the save outcome, but the d20 was still rolled (for parity with the existing broadcast contract — tests assert on `rolled`, `total`, `bonus`). The breakdown now reads "save would have been 1d20[18]+2 = 20 vs DC 10" — a passing roll, but RAW dropped concentration anyway. The GM can see at a glance whether the death was bad luck (failed both) or RAW-driven (would have passed but 0 HP). The 💀 emoji is the "this is RAW, not a dice failure" tell.
**Description (cont 3):** Why test_failed_con_save_still_emits_heart_log uses a retry loop. The non-0-HP CON save is genuinely random (d20 vs DC); to assert the 💔 log still appears, the test needs at least one failed save in the run. Rowan has no CON-save proficiency so P(fail | DC=15) ≈ 70%; 15 retries gives ~1 - 0.30^15 ≈ 99.999% chance of at least one failure. Same pattern as the existing v2.39.0 `test_concentration_break_emits_gm_only_log`.
**Description (cont 4):** Why test_roll_3_failures_emits_skull_log uses a retry loop instead of dice seeding. The TEST_MODE `/api/test/dice/seed` endpoint takes a single integer seed, not a forced d20 value. Finding a seed that produces three sub-DC rolls in a row is empirical + brittle to RNG implementation. Retry loop with 15 attempts (each: reset to dying/2-failures + re-hex + roll) has P(roll-fails | no-CON-prof) = 11/20 = 55%; ~99.99% chance of at least one death within 15 attempts. Reset overhead per loop is ~30ms (4 HTTP calls).
**Description (cont 5):** Verification. Ran the new tests pre-fix: `test_override_to_dead_emits_skull_log` failed (note started with 💔, breakdown said "✗ Failed" not "GM override"). Post-fix: all 4 pass. Full regression: 234 harness tests pass (was 230, +4 new); 33 encounter-sim tests still pass (no broadcast-shape break).

## [2.49.49] - 2026-05-21

**Schema version:** 56
**Commit summary:** **Fix RAW bug: death-save state transitions didn't drop the caster's concentration.** Eighth application-side bug surfaced by the encounter-sim test suite. The v2.49.48 commit closed the 0-HP damage path (`_maybe_concentration_save` force-drops at 0 HP), but two adjacent endpoints sat outside that helper and still left concentration installed on dying / dead PCs: **(a)** `POST /character/{cid}/death-save` (rolling) — when a PC rolls 3 failures and dies, no damage event fires, no save runs through `_maybe_concentration_save`. **(b)** `POST /character/{cid}/death-save/override` — the GM force-sets status to dying / stable / dead with no damage or save. Both are real RAW gaps: PHB p.203 says concentration ends when the caster is incapacitated or killed regardless of how they got there. Fix: new `_drop_caster_concentration(campaign_id, character_id)` helper that scans the combatant's buffs for any with `concentration=True` and removes each via the existing `_remove_buff` cascade (which handles paired buff cleanup + sheet mirror + broadcast). Hooked into `roll_death_save` when `new_status == "dead"` and into `override_death_save` whenever the GM sets status to dying / stable / dead. 3 new harness tests pin both branches + a guard against over-broad firing on `status="alive"`. PATCH — bug fix; reuses the existing `buff_update` broadcast shape.
**Description:** Two edits. **(1)** `app/routes/tabletop_routes.py` — added `_drop_caster_concentration(campaign_id, character_id) -> int` helper near the existing `_drop_paired_concentration_buffs` cluster. It looks up the combatant by `char_id` in the live battle state, collects the keys of any buffs flagged `concentration: True`, and calls `_remove_buff` for each. Returns the count for telemetry / tests. Called from `roll_death_save` post-`_set_death_save_state` when the new status is "dead". Called from `override_death_save` whenever the incoming status is one of dying / stable / dead. **(2)** `tests/harness/test_death_save_drops_concentration.py` (NEW) — 3 tests: `test_override_to_dead_drops_concentration` (override(dead) on Hex'd Magnus → buff_update without hex + live /buffs confirms), `test_roll_3_failures_drops_concentration` (dying Magnus → override(failures=3, status=dead) → same broadcast assertion; uses override to drive the 3-failures transition deterministically since rolling three sub-DC d20s in a row needs careful seed selection), `test_override_to_alive_does_not_drop_concentration` (guard against over-broad fix — alive → alive transitions don't drop the buff).
**Description (cont):** Why two hook points, not one. The two endpoints share the underlying `_set_death_save_state` writer, but they take different paths INTO it: `roll_death_save` reads the current state, rolls a d20, decides the new status; `override_death_save` takes the status directly from the request body. Hooking into `_set_death_save_state` itself would be tempting (one site = fewer call sites to forget) but that helper is also called during the alive→alive idempotent path, and a top-down hook there would either over-fire (drop concentration when status doesn't actually change) or need a "did status transition?" check that duplicates the caller's logic. Cleaner to call the helper at the two endpoints where the transition has been COMMITTED and the new status is known.
**Description (cont 2):** Why `override(stable)` also drops. RAW: "stable" means the PC is unconscious at 0 HP but not actively dying — they're still incapacitated, so concentration ends. Pre-fix the override path could install Hex on an alive PC, then GM-override them to stable, and Hex would stay. The new firing condition is `status_in in ("dying", "stable", "dead")` covering all three incapacitated states; `status="alive"` is excluded so a healing override doesn't trigger unnecessary buff cleanup.
**Description (cont 3):** Why the rolled-3-failures test uses override(failures=3, status=dead) rather than rolling three d20s. Magnus has no CON-save proficiency so the death-save is raw 1d20 < 10. Forcing three sub-10 outcomes in a row through the dice-seed endpoint would need a specific seed sequence; the seed search is fiddly and brittle to dice-generator changes. The override path exercises the SAME `_drop_caster_concentration` code branch with deterministic input. The `roll_death_save` branch is itself covered indirectly because both endpoints route through the same helper — and `tests/harness/test_death_save.py` already pins the d20 mechanics.
**Description (cont 4):** Verification. Ran the new tests pre-fix: `test_override_to_dead_drops_concentration` failed at the `buff_update` assertion (no broadcast fired, hex stayed installed). Ran post-fix: all 3 pass. Full regression: 230 harness tests pass (was 227, +3 new); 33 encounter-sim tests pass (no regression). Eight bugs surfaced + fixed by encounter-sim so far.

### Fixed
- `app/routes/tabletop_routes.py::roll_death_save` — when a death-save roll transitions the PC to status=dead, calls the new `_drop_caster_concentration` helper.
- `app/routes/tabletop_routes.py::override_death_save` — when the override sets status to dying / stable / dead, calls `_drop_caster_concentration`.

### Added
- `app/routes/tabletop_routes.py::_drop_caster_concentration(campaign_id, character_id) -> int` — scans the live battle combatant for buffs flagged `concentration=True` and removes each via `_remove_buff`. Returns the count.
- `tests/harness/test_death_save_drops_concentration.py` — 3 tests covering the override(dead) branch, the rolled-3-failures branch (via override-driven status transition), and the override(alive) negative-control branch.
- `docs/test-harness-coverage.md` — catalog entry for the new test file; total 227 → 230.

### Notes
- **Backward compat.** Pure additive — reuses the existing `buff_update` broadcast shape (no new fields). Clients that already consume `buff_update` on buff removal will see hex / hunter's-mark / hold-person disappear from the buff list when the caster dies; that's the intended visible behavior.
- **Eight bugs fixed by encounter-sim so far**: v2.49.40 (force_gm_sync NPC damage), v2.49.41 (DELETE concentration paired-buffs), v2.49.42 (PATCH sheet-fields HP broadcast), v2.49.45 (hp_update handler renderBattle), v2.49.46 (death_save handler renderBattle), v2.49.47 (heal_applied handler renderBattle), v2.49.48 (RAW 0-HP concentration drop), v2.49.49 (this commit — death-save state transitions drop concentration).

### Filed
- **UI tag for "concentration ended by incapacitation"** — the existing `forced_drop_on_zero_hp` field (v2.49.48) and this commit's death-save-driven drops both end up in the buff list as a removed buff. The UI doesn't currently distinguish "concentration ended because you died" from "you ended it voluntarily" or "you failed a CON save." A future commit could add a narrative roll-log entry on death-induced drops (`💀 NAME lost concentration on SPELL — incapacitated`) similar to the v2.39.0 break log.
- **Knocked-out via non-damage incapacitation** — sleep, hold person on the caster, banishment, etc. also incapacitate without dropping HP. Those should also drop the target's own concentration. Out of scope for this commit (needs a separate audit of every condition-applying endpoint to find which ones imply incapacitation); filed as a follow-up.

## [2.49.48] - 2026-05-21

**Schema version:** 56
**Commit summary:** **Fix RAW bug: concentration didn't end automatically at 0 HP.** Seventh application-side bug surfaced by the encounter-sim test suite. PHB p.203: "you also lose concentration on a spell if you are incapacitated or killed." Pre-fix, ``_maybe_concentration_save`` rolled the CON save unconditionally — a PC who took damage dropping to 0 HP could PASS the save and remain concentrating on Hex / Hunter's Mark / Hold Person / Spirit Guardians while dying or dead. The encounter-sim ``test_drops_on_zero_hp`` (v2.49.25) worked around this by inflating ``damage_amount`` to 65 (DC=32, impossible to pass) — the workaround documented the bug but didn't fix it. Fix: in ``_maybe_concentration_save``, snapshot the post-damage ``hp.current``; if it's 0 (or negative), force ``passed=False`` regardless of the d20 + add ``forced_drop_on_zero_hp: True`` to the broadcast for telemetry. The existing ``_remove_buff`` path runs, dropping the buff + cascading paired cleanup. The encounter-sim workaround can also drop the inflated damage back to a normal value — done in this commit. 2 new harness tests + 1 updated encounter-sim test pin both branches. PATCH — bug fix; the broadcast gains a ``forced_drop_on_zero_hp`` field (additive, defaults to False on the normal path).
**Description:** Three edits + 1 new file. **(1)** `app/routes/tabletop_routes.py::_maybe_concentration_save` — snapshot ``hp.current`` after the existing damage application, compute ``forced_drop_on_zero_hp = hp_current_after <= 0``. Compute ``passed = (total >= dc) and not forced_drop_on_zero_hp``. Add the flag to the broadcast payload. The save is still ROLLED at 0 HP (kept for telemetry parity — the GM sees what the save WOULD have been) but the outcome is overridden. **(2)** `tests/harness/test_concentration_drops_on_zero_hp.py` (NEW) — 2 tests: (a) Magnus drops to 0 HP via damage_amount=15 (DC=10, passable); asserts ``forced_drop_on_zero_hp=True`` + ``passed=False`` + ``dropped_key="hex"``; (b) Magnus takes 13 damage to HP 20 (not 0); asserts ``forced_drop_on_zero_hp=False`` + ``passed`` follows the d20. **(3)** `tests/encounter_sim/level_3_edge_cases/concentration/test_drops_on_zero_hp.py` — damage tuning relaxed from 65 → 33 (full HP to 0) now that the forced-drop rule guarantees Hex drops without DC gymnastics. Comment captures the workaround history. **(4)** `docs/test-harness-coverage.md` — new entry for the test file; total 225 → 227.
**Description (cont):** Why a new ``forced_drop_on_zero_hp`` field instead of just relying on ``passed=False``. Two reasons. (a) Telemetry / UX. The roll-log card currently renders "❌ Concentration save failed" on a fail. A 0-HP forced drop is conceptually different — the save WAS rolled and may have been a 20, but the rule says concentration ends regardless. Future UI can render "💀 Concentration broken (0 HP)" or similar, distinguished by the flag. (b) Backward compat. Existing client handlers + tests that only look at ``passed`` continue to behave correctly (the chip drops either way); the flag is purely additive metadata.
**Description (cont 2):** Why we still roll the d20 in the forced case. Could short-circuit and skip the roll, but rolling preserves the broadcast contract (existing tests assert on ``rolled``, ``total``, ``bonus`` fields) AND gives the GM auditable telemetry — "the save would have been a 19, but RAW dropped concentration anyway." Cost is one ``random.randint(1, 20)`` call per drop. Negligible.
**Description (cont 3):** How the encounter-sim suite surfaced this. ``test_drops_on_zero_hp`` (v2.49.25) was the first test that tried to assert "concentration drops on 0 HP." First write used damage_amount=33 (full HP → 0); the test was flaky because Magnus's CON+2 save sometimes passed against DC=16. The workaround was to inflate damage_amount to 65 (DC=32, unpassable). The CHANGELOG entry at v2.49.25 documented this as a tuning choice; this commit recognizes it as papering over a real RAW gap and fixes the underlying rule. With the fix, damage_amount=33 works deterministically — the test was simplified back to that value.
**Description (cont 4):** Verification. Ran the new harness tests pre-fix: ``test_concentration_force_drops_at_zero_hp`` failed (concentration was rolled, ``passed`` could be True). Ran post-fix: both pass. 227 harness tests pass (was 225, +2 new); 33 encounter-sim tests pass with the simplified damage value.

### Fixed
- `app/routes/tabletop_routes.py::_maybe_concentration_save` — force-drops concentration when caster's HP is 0 (RAW PHB p.203). Adds ``forced_drop_on_zero_hp`` field to the ``concentration_save`` broadcast.

### Added
- `tests/harness/test_concentration_drops_on_zero_hp.py` — 2 tests covering the forced-drop branch + the normal-save branch.
- `docs/test-harness-coverage.md` — catalog entry; total 225 → 227.

### Changed
- `tests/encounter_sim/level_3_edge_cases/concentration/test_drops_on_zero_hp.py` — `damage_amount` reduced from 65 (workaround for the bug) to 33 (the actual full-HP-to-0 amount). Comment captures the history.

### Notes
- **Backward compat.** Pure additive — `forced_drop_on_zero_hp` is a new field, defaults to False on the normal save path. Existing clients that don't read the field continue to work.
- **Seven bugs fixed by encounter-sim so far**: v2.49.40 (force_gm_sync NPC damage), v2.49.41 (DELETE concentration paired-buffs), v2.49.42 (PATCH sheet-fields HP broadcast), v2.49.45 (hp_update handler renderBattle), v2.49.46 (death_save handler renderBattle), v2.49.47 (heal_applied handler renderBattle), v2.49.48 (this commit — RAW 0-HP concentration drop).

### Filed
- **UI tag for forced drop** — when the roll-log card renders concentration-save outcomes, distinguish ``forced_drop_on_zero_hp=True`` from a regular failed save (e.g. "💀 Concentration broken (0 HP)" vs "❌ Concentration save failed (DC X)"). Today both render the same; the flag enables the distinction but no UI consumes it yet.
- **`/death-save` rolled-3-failures path** — when a PC dies from rolling 3 death-save failures (not from instakill), is their concentration also dropped? The RAW "incapacitated" trigger applies at 0 HP regardless of how they got there, so the existing forced-drop fix covers it via the damage_amount > 0 entry condition... but death-saves don't go through ``_maybe_concentration_save`` at all. Worth a follow-up audit + test.

Fixes the case where an NPC buff (Paralyzed from Hold Person, Frightened from Fear) is installed but the GM's view of the chip doesn't update until the next push. **(2)** `app/routes/tabletop_routes.py::_drop_paired_concentration_buffs` (line 745) — same fix. Pre-fix: `PATCH /api/campaign/{cid}/character/{cid}/sheet-fields` only broadcast `character_death_save` when `hp_result["status_changed"]` — i.e. on transitions into / out of dying / stable / dead. A vanilla HP change within "alive" (e.g. GM sets a PC's HP from 35 to 25 via the sheet edit panel, or a test PATCHes HP for setup) fired NO broadcast. Non-GM clients had no signal to update their local `window.battle.combatants[…].hp_current`, so Alice's HP-bar view stayed stale until something else triggered a state refresh. Surfaced by the encounter-sim `test_alice_observes_hp_update` (v2.49.35) which originally tried PATCH /sheet-fields and got no broadcast — the test was rewritten to use /attack to find one. With the fix landed, both paths broadcast `character_hp_update`. Fix: snapshot `pre_patch_current_hp` before `_apply_hp_change`; after the existing `character_death_save` (still fires on status change), broadcast `character_hp_update` whenever `new_current != pre_patch_current_hp`. Uses the same shape `_apply_damage_to_combatant` uses — same client handler at tabletop.js:3102 (no IS_GM guard). 3 new harness tests pin the broadcast contract; total harness 222 → 225. PATCH — bug fix; no schema or API contract change.
**Description:** Three edits. **(1)** `app/routes/tabletop_routes.py::patch_sheet_fields` — snapshot `pre_patch_current_hp = int(existing_hp.get("current") or 0)` before mutating the sheet, then after the conditional `character_death_save` broadcast, emit `character_hp_update` whenever HP actually changed. Suppressed if `new_current == pre_patch_current_hp` so no-op PATCHes (settings-form HP=HP) don't spam the WS channel. Source label `"sheet_patch"` distinguishes from `"attack"` / `"undo_attack"` / `"heal"` sources. **(2)** `tests/harness/test_sheet_patch_hp_broadcast.py` (NEW) — 3 tests covering: HP-down within alive broadcasts with negative delta, HP-up (heal) broadcasts with positive delta, no-op PATCH suppresses the broadcast. **(3)** `docs/test-harness-coverage.md` — catalog entry for the new test file; total count 222 → 225.
**Description (cont):** Why character_hp_update is the right broadcast type (not a new one). The existing `character_hp_update` already covers PC HP changes from `_apply_damage_to_combatant` (`/attack`, `/cast_spell`) and `_apply_heal_to_combatant` (heal endpoints). The client handler at tabletop.js:3102 already mutates `window.battle.combatants[…].hp_current` AND `charById[…].hp_current` AND triggers a canvas re-render (the v2.49.4 skull overlay rides on this same render pass). PATCH /sheet-fields had been the ONE damage / heal path NOT broadcasting it — closing that gap unifies all HP-change paths under one broadcast.
**Description (cont 2):** Why suppress the no-op broadcast. The settings page submits PATCH /sheet-fields with the full sheet body on every save — even unrelated edits like "rename a feat" arrive with `hp: {current: 35}` because the form serializer doesn't know which fields changed. Without the no-op suppression, every settings save would spam `character_hp_update` to every client. The `new_current != pre_patch_current_hp` guard kills the spam path; only ACTUAL HP changes fire the broadcast.
**Description (cont 3):** Verification. Ran the new tests BEFORE the fix landed (all 3 failed — no broadcast); ran AFTER (all 3 pass). 225 harness tests pass; 32 encounter-sim tests still pass (no regressions). ### Added

  - `test_hp_heal_broadcasts_positive_delta` — HP up fires with positive delta.

### Changed
- `docs/test-harness-coverage.md` — new catalog entry; total tests 222 → 225.

### Notes

## [2.49.40] - 2026-05-21

**Schema version:** 56
**Commit summary:** **Fix bug discovered by encounter-sim: NPC damage broadcasts lack `force_gm_sync`, causing GM-side state drift after every monster attack.** First application-side bug fix surfaced by the new encounter-sim test suite. Pre-fix: when an NPC takes damage from `/attack`, `/cast_spell`, or `/undo_attack_damage`, the server mutates the hub's battle state, persists it, and broadcasts `battle_update` — BUT without the `force_gm_sync: True` flag. The GM client's broadcast handler (tabletop.html:5543) refuses plain `battle_update` broadcasts under the v2.5.5 echo-loop guard, so the GM's local `window.battle.combatants[…]` stays at the pre-damage HP value. As soon as the GM does anything that triggers `pushBattle()` — drag a token, edit init, click "Next Turn" — their stale local state overwrites the server's correctly-updated HP. The bandit visually "comes back to life" the moment the GM moves a token. The encounter-sim Phase 1 PoCs ALL had to assert layer-6 (init-tracker HP DOM) against the response body's `target_hp_after` instead of the rendered DOM, because the GM driver couldn't see the post-damage state. Fix: add `force_gm_sync: True` to the two affected broadcasts in `_apply_damage_to_combatant` (NPC branch, line 1147) and the `/undo_attack_damage` NPC path (line 12624). Mirrors the v2.48.8 `/place_aoe` pattern at line 7986 which already broadcasts correctly. New harness test `tests/harness/test_attack_force_gm_sync.py` (1 test) pins the broadcast shape; total harness tests 221 → 222. PATCH — bug fix; no schema or API contract change.
**Description:** Three edits. **(1)** `app/routes/tabletop_routes.py:1147` (the `_apply_damage_to_combatant` NPC-branch broadcast) — added `"force_gm_sync": True` to the broadcast dict. Comment cites the v2.5.5 guard, the v2.48.8 mirror pattern, and the encounter-sim Phase 1 GM-driver caveat that surfaced the bug. **(2)** `app/routes/tabletop_routes.py:12624` (the `/undo_attack_damage` NPC path's broadcast) — same fix. Without this the undo would "not work" in the GM's view until they pushed something else. **(3)** `tests/harness/test_attack_force_gm_sync.py` (NEW) — `test_npc_damage_broadcast_carries_force_gm_sync` seeds Krieger + Bandit Alpha, fires `/attack`, asserts the `battle_update` broadcast carries `force_gm_sync: True` AND the broadcasted state contains the post-damage HP. Defensive: skips the assertion gracefully if Krieger misses (no broadcast in that case).
**Description (cont):** Why no client-side fix instead. Two options were considered: (a) add the flag to the broadcast (this commit), (b) remove the IS_GM gate from the broadcast handler so the GM accepts all `battle_update`s. Option (b) was rejected because the gate has a real purpose — it prevents echo loops when the GM pushes state via `pushBattle()` and would otherwise immediately receive their own push back, mid-edit. The right fix is server-authoritative: the server tags broadcasts that came from server-side computation (damage, undo) with `force_gm_sync: True` because those are NOT echo-back events. Broadcasts that originated from `pushBattle` (the GM's own PUT) leave the flag off so the gate works.
**Description (cont 2):** How the encounter-sim suite surfaced this. Phase 1 commit C (`test_garrik_strike`, v2.49.16) tried to assert layer 6 ("Bandit Alpha's HP in init tracker reflects damage") on the GM driver. The DOM never updated. Investigation found tabletop.html:5543's echo-loop guard. Workaround: assert on response body's `target_hp_after` instead of DOM. That workaround was documented in the test docstring and carried forward to every subsequent PoC test. The "fix this in the server" item was filed in the v2.49.16 CHANGELOG "### Filed" section as: "**Force-GM-sync from /attack?** — Investigate whether /attack should broadcast a follow-up battle_update with force_gm_sync: True so the GM's init tracker stays in sync with the server-applied damage. Today the GM's local state drifts until they pushBattle, which can overwrite server-applied damage on the next manual edit. The fix would mirror the /place_aoe pattern at v2.48.8 (line 7986 of tabletop_routes.py). Separate from the encounter-sim suite, but the suite is what surfaced it." This commit IS that fix.
**Description (cont 3):** What the fix enables on the test side. With this commit landing, the encounter-sim Phase 1/2 GM-driver tests CAN now assert on DOM-HP-drop instead of response-body workarounds. The existing tests still pass (their response-body assertions are still valid); a future cleanup commit can swap them to DOM assertions and remove the docstring caveats. Filed.
**Description (cont 4):** Why CLAUDE.md compliance. Per the harness-test-per-endpoint rule, a broadcast shape change (new field on `battle_update`) requires a harness test. New file `test_attack_force_gm_sync.py` covers it. Verification: 222 harness tests pass (was 221); 32 encounter-sim tests still pass (no regressions); the new test fails BEFORE the fix landed (verified mid-development) and passes AFTER.

### Fixed
- `app/routes/tabletop_routes.py::_apply_damage_to_combatant` (NPC branch, line 1147) — broadcast now carries `force_gm_sync: True`. GM client picks up NPC HP changes from `/attack` and `/cast_spell` without state drift.
- `app/routes/tabletop_routes.py::undo_attack_damage` (NPC path, line 12624) — same fix for the undo path. Undo "actually works" in the GM's view immediately, no longer requires another action to flush.

### Added
- `tests/harness/test_attack_force_gm_sync.py` — 1 test: `test_npc_damage_broadcast_carries_force_gm_sync`. Pins the broadcast shape.

**Schema version:** 56
**Commit summary:** **Encounter-sim Phase 4 commit Q — concentration cleanup subsystem opener: `test_save_on_damage`.** Opens the concentration-cleanup test family (6 plan items). Validates the **damage-triggered concentration save** path: a concentrating caster takes damage → server fires CON save at `DC = max(10, damage/2)` → on fail, the concentration buff drops + a `buff_update` follows; on pass, concentration holds. Complementary to commit L's `test_concentration_lifecycle` (install + manual DELETE end): there the end was caller-driven, here it's automatic on damage. Test uses Magnus's Hex with 10 damage (DC=10, Magnus rolls CON save). The pass / fail branch is selected by the WS frame's `passed` field rather than hardcoded — the test asserts self-consistent behavior regardless of which roll outcome the dice produce. New subdirectory `level_3_edge_cases/concentration/`. PATCH — additive test only; reuses `apply_damage` + `post_use` helpers from commits J/P. Full encounter-sim suite at 23 tests / ~40 s × 5 runs, no flake.
**Description:** Two new files. **(1)** `tests/encounter_sim/level_3_edge_cases/concentration/__init__.py` (empty package shell). **(2)** `tests/encounter_sim/level_3_edge_cases/concentration/test_save_on_damage.py` — the test. Long-rests Magnus (Hex consumes a Pact slot; refill so the slot is available), installs Hex on Pip via `post_use("cast_hex", ...)`, waits for `buff_update` carrying the hex buff, asserts the chip is visible. Then applies 10 damage to Magnus via `apply_damage(magnus_id, damage_amount=10, new_hp_current=23)`. Waits for `concentration_save` broadcast filtered by `character_id == magnus.id`, asserts `buff_key=="hex"`, `damage_amount==10`, `dc==10`, `passed` is a bool. Branches on `passed`: if False, waits for the `buff_update` carrying either `removed_key=="hex"` OR a buffs list without hex (server has both broadcast shapes for this path; accept either), then asserts the chip is gone via `expect(...).to_have_count(0)`. If True, asserts the chip is still visible. Either branch is a valid outcome — the test exercises the concentration-save BROADCAST shape regardless and the DOM-update CONSEQUENCE conditional on outcome.
**Description (cont):** Why both broadcast shapes are accepted on the fail branch. The server has two paths that fire buff_update after a failed concentration save: (a) the full new buff list with hex removed, (b) a diff-style frame with `removed_key`. Different code paths in `tabletop_routes.py` use different shapes depending on whether other buffs needed to be touched simultaneously. The test accepts EITHER signal because both convey the same semantic — "hex is no longer installed on Magnus." Tightening to one specific shape would create a regression sensitivity to refactors that aren't user-visible. The DOM-level assertion (chip gone) is the user-visible contract; the WS shape is implementation detail.
**Description (cont 2):** Why the test doesn't seed dice for a known outcome. Could force a fail branch by seeding `set_dice_seed(2)` (likely produces a low roll that fails the DC 10 save). But then the test only ever exercises ONE branch — the OTHER branch's behavior would silently regress without coverage. By running unseeded, the test will see PASS sometimes and FAIL sometimes across the CI run history, exercising both branches over time. The branches are short enough that running both each test would be cheap, but they need slightly different state setup; the conditional-branching approach lets one test cover both with no setup cost.
**Description (cont 3):** Why no harness test. Test-only addition exercising existing endpoint + broadcast behavior (covered by `tests/harness/test_concentration_buffs.py::test_concentration_save_on_damage`). The UI-layer addition here is the chip-removal DOM assertion which the harness doesn't reach. Verification: 5 sequential local runs × 23 tests pass at ~40 s/run, no flake.
